title: Man. Post. Cap. IX: PLAC — 'Adam sinned for all posterity': true as great harm; false as loco nostro
pass_a_gloss: Placeus splits Garrigues's 'Adam sinned for all posterity': true if it means great harm birthing the race's death-bound vice; false and careless if it means Adam sinned in our place (loco nostro).
pass_b_english: Still less do I grasp what you add: when Adam sinned, he sinned for all his posterity. If you mean he sinned to the great harm of all his posterity, nothing is truer. For from that was born the vice that invaded the human race and devoted it to death. But if you mean he sinned in our place, nothing less carefully considered could have been said by you.
source_text: Minus etiam capio quae subnectis, cum Adamus peccavit, pro omnibus suis posteris peccavit. Si intelligis eum magno omnium posterorum malo peccasse, nihil verius. Hinc enim natum est vitium illud quod genus humanum invasit & morti addixit. Sed si intelligis eum loco nostro peccavisse, nihil dici potuit a te minus considerate.

choices.choice: True as harm; false as loco nostro

notes: Cap. IX pro-posteris densify section 635 from locked 1661 Latin (pp. 353–354 tip).
